parties: Max Estates Limited (parent/acquirer) acquires equity shares in Max Square Limited (subsidiary) via CCD conversion
headline: Max Estates Limited acquires equity shares in subsidiary Max Square Limited pursuant to CCD conversion
sum: Max Estates Limited has converted Convertible Cumulative Debentures (CCDs) into equity shares in its subsidiary Max Square Limited. The acquisition was disclosed to the NSE on 12 August 2026 as a general update.
implication: Parent-to-subsidiary CCD conversion mechanics highlight the use of debt instruments as internal capital restructuring tools; review Companies Act 2013 Sch. VI valuation norms and SEBI DIP guidelines on related-party pricing where parent converts instruments at conversion terms.
detail: Max Estates Limited, a real estate developer (subsidiary of Max Healthcare in the Max group), announced the acquisition of equity shares in its own subsidiary Max Square Limited (engaged in real estate development) pursuant to the automatic or optional conversion of CCDs previously held by Max Estates. The transaction was disclosed via NSE regulatory announcement under the Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements (LODR). No consideration amount is disclosed in the public filing; the conversion mechanics and valuation would be determined by the original CCD instrument terms and Companies Act 2013 Schedule VI valuation norms for related-party transactions.

framework.note: Related-party transaction valuation; conversion of debt into equity by parent in subsidiary is a related-party transaction requiring fair valuation and potential shareholder/board approval
Acquisition of shares by a company in its own subsidiary; registration and reporting requirements
Disclosure of material events and milestones; acquisition of shares in subsidiary must be notified to stock exchange within 30 minutes of approval or disclosure
Additional scrutiny on related-party deals by listed entities; parent-subsidiary share acquisitions may require independent director approval
Private company exemptions; if Max Square Limited is a private subsidiary, certain filing and approval requirements may be relaxed
If CCD conversion entails a gift or shortfall consideration, gift tax implications under s. 56(2)(vii) may apply; ensure valuation supports no shortfall for tax purposes
If any cross-border capital element exists in the parent-subsidiary chain, FEMA compliance for inbound investment or repatriation required
Loans and investments by a company in its subsidiaries; if funded by fresh capital, investment limits apply

structure.consideration: Not disclosed; determined by original CCD instrument terms and schedule VI valuation
conditions: Conversion terms as stipulated in original CCD instrument
Compliance with Companies Act 2013 Schedule VI related-party transaction valuation
Board and/or shareholder approval (if required under related-party transaction regime)
approvals: Board of Directors approval (Max Estates Limited)
Regulatory disclosure to NSE/BSE under LODR Reg. 30
structure.novel: Subsidiary-level CCD conversion; internal capital restructuring within Max Estates group to convert debenture holdings into equity ownership stake in Max Square Limited without external capital injection.
